summary.text: Robb Ryerse is the Democratic nominee for Arkansas's 3rd Congressional District. A pastor and nonprofit leader who lives in Springdale, he ran against Rep. Steve Womack in the 2018 Republican primary and has since worked with Vote Common Good and co-founded Vortex PAC. His campaign website describes the race as not being about Democrats or Republicans, and he runs on a platform he describes as "Faith: Powered, Family: Protected, Freedom: Preserved," covering democracy reform, healthcare, and civil rights.

paragraphs.text: Ryerse is a pastor and nonprofit leader who, according to his campaign website, has lived in Springdale for 20 years with his wife, Vanessa; they raised four children and started a church called Vintage Fellowship.
He was a founder and co-pastor of Vintage Fellowship in Fayetteville and, as of 2017, also held a full-time job with the shopper marketing agency 3 Tier Logic, according to Talk Business & Politics.
He entered the 2018 Republican primary for the 3rd District with the backing of the group Brand New Congress and lost to Womack on May 22, 2018.
Since 2018, Ryerse has worked with Vote Common Good and co-founded Vortex PAC with Dr. Chris Jones, according to his campaign website.
He advanced as the Democratic nominee for 2026 after the March 3 Democratic primary was canceled.

sources.title: Pastor plans GOP primary challenge to Rep. Womack, running on 'Brand New Congress' platform
